subject.title: [Feature]: Let Apple Watch connect as a direct Gateway node

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-party, opt-in Apple Watch direct Gateway node, and what bounded auth/capability surface should it expose?
rationale: The existing seams make the idea plausible, but shipping it changes Apple Watch product scope and creates a new device credential, setup, revocation, and node-capability boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Sponsor bounded direct Watch node
options.body: Proceed with a foreground-only direct Watch node that uses a watch-scoped credential, secure reachable Gateway URL, explicit forget/revoke UX, and unchanged iPhone relay fallback.

options.title: Keep Watch relay-only for now
options.body: Reject direct Watch Gateway access for this cycle and keep Watch behavior dependent on the paired iPhone until maintainers want to expand watchOS scope.

options.title: Request a design spike first
options.body: Ask for a short technical design and proof plan before accepting implementation, especially for token handoff, Canvas browser behavior, and fallback semantics.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded direct Watch node
recommendation.body: Proceed with a foreground-only direct Watch node that uses a watch-scoped credential, secure reachable Gateway URL, explicit forget/revoke UX, and unchanged iPhone relay fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored recent merged watch feature work and opened this issue with the product/security constraints that need confirmation.
